message.content: In lions, the most conspicuous dominant genetic trait is the allele that produces the typical tawny coat color. This allele is carried on the MC1R (melanocortin‑1 receptor) gene, which determines the distribution and intensity of eumelanin (black pigment) versus pheomelanin (yellow/red pigment). The dominant MC1R allele suppresses excess eumelanin production, resulting in the characteristic light‑brown, tawny fur that is seen in most adult lions.
